edges.mechanism: Additive impairment of hemostasis; any bleeding OR 1.36 (RCTs) and 1.42 (observational) for OAC+aspirin vs OAC alone.

Ibuprofen dosed before aspirin competitively blocks irreversible platelet COX-1 acetylation, abolishing aspirin's antiplatelet effect. FDA: take ibuprofen 400 mg >=30 min after or >=8 h before immediate-release aspirin; no advice possible for enteric-coated aspirin.
edges.evidence: Crossover PD study (NEJM 2001); FDA science paper and label

edges.mechanism: Additive GI bleeding and renal impairment; ibuprofen and naproxen interfere with low-dose aspirin's platelet COX-1 inhibition (diclofenac, acetaminophen did not).
edges.evidence: Observational MA; PD studies; FDA/DailyMed labels

edges.mechanism: Additive GI bleeding risk; GI bleeding aHR 1.27 among aspirin users taking SSRIs (paroxetine aHR 1.73).
edges.evidence: Prospective cohort (UK Biobank) and observational MA

edges.mechanism: PPIs lower aspirin-associated upper GI bleeding (RR 0.30 vs placebo); pantoprazole reduced bleeding gastroduodenal lesions (HR 0.52). Possible increase in lower GI bleeding from non-randomized data.
edges.evidence: MA of 16 RCTs + 14 non-RCTs; large RCT (COMPASS)

edges.mechanism: Salicylate may reduce renal methotrexate clearance (label: bone marrow toxicity, especially elderly/renal impairment); PK data mixed and low-dose aspirin showed no effect on high-dose MTX elimination.
edges.evidence: Label, small PK study, cohort, Cochrane review

edges.mechanism: Theoretical additive antiplatelet effect; MA of 11 RCTs found no overall bleeding increase and no modification by background antiplatelet therapy; high-dose purified EPA raised bleeding modestly.
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs (n=120,643); retrospective cohort on fish oil + DAPT

edges.mechanism: Vitamin E increased haemorrhagic stroke risk (RR 1.22); combined with aspirin's ICH risk (RR 1.33) bleeding risks may add; vitamin E gave no CV benefit on top of aspirin.
edges.evidence: MA of RCTs; factorial RCT (PPP); additive risk inferred

edges.mechanism: Garlic has antiplatelet activity; garlic tablets did not change aggregation but 30% at 3 tablets/day reported bleeding.
Aged garlic extract showed no excess bleeding with warfarin in a small RCT; data with aspirin lacking.
Garlic component has antiplatelet activity; additive bleeding with aspirin is theoretical.
In-vitro antiplatelet activity of turmeric; Meriva curcumin did not change bleeding time over 10 days on aspirin.
Turmeric reduces platelet aggregation in vitro; clinical additive bleeding not demonstrated.
Ginger reduces platelet aggregation in human studies and potentiates other antiplatelet effects; additive bleeding with aspirin plausible.
edges.evidence: Narrative review; small human PD study

edges.mechanism: Contains ginger and curcumin, both with antiplatelet signals; additive effect with aspirin plausible but unquantified.
Green tea catechins inhibit platelet aggregation in vitro; green tea interacts with warfarin.
Ginseng reduces platelet aggregation; additive antiplatelet effect with aspirin is theoretical.
COX-inhibition-triggered bronchospasm, urticaria, angioedema in asthma with nasal polyps; ~7% of adult asthmatics, ~15% of severe asthma.

edges.mechanism: Oxidative hemolysis reported, including late-onset hemolysis on 100 mg/day followed by fatal subdural hemorrhage; safety data contradictory.
Low-dose aspirin reduces renal urate excretion; recurrent gout attack OR 1.81 (1.91 at <=100 mg/d), nullified by allopurinol.
True physiological rise in serum urate and fall in urate excretion (~15%) at 75 mg/day; a 2-week RCT subanalysis found no rise.
Aspirin suppresses serum TXB2, arachidonic-acid aggregation, VerifyNow Aspirin; 'resistance' results disagree across assays and enteric coating causes pseudoresistance.
High salicylate falsely raises chloride on direct ion-selective electrodes, producing normal/negative anion gap that masks salicylate toxicity.
